items.title: Supreme Court adjourns Delhi protest pleas to Oct 15; compliance-affidavit deadline extended
items.summary: Bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was to hear the Delhi protest petitions (CEC/SIR row) today, but Justice Mohana's ill-health meant adjournment to Oct 15 with the parties' consent. On SG Tushar Mehta's request, the deadline for the compliance report under the Oct 9 order (metro/train services) and responses to Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt petition and Menaka Guruswamy's petition was extended to Oct 15. Sr Advs Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, CU Singh, Nitya Ramakrishnan and Indira Jaising appeared.

items.title: SC seeks senior Delhi Police officer's presence over alleged assault of women journalists during protest coverage
items.summary: CJI Surya Kant, after Sr Adv Indira Jaising mentioned a petition by the Network of Women in Media, India (NWMI) seeking safeguards for journalists (especially women) covering protests, said the Court wanted a senior police official present to explain the allegations; the petition will be heard Thursday alongside the alleged-police-action matter. Sr Adv Gopal Sankaranarayanan separately mentioned a Free Speech Collective contempt petition alleging police assaulted journalists in breach of the Court's Oct 10 order protecting mediapersons; Sr Adv Chander Uday Singh raised a similar petition.

items.title: SC issues notice on ADR petition challenging Section 16 immunity for CEC and ECs
items.summary: The Court issued notice on a fresh petition by the Association for Democratic Reforms challenging Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioners and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which bars civil or criminal proceedings against the CEC and Election Commissioners for acts done in discharge of official duty. Background: on Oct 5 the Court had orally observed that this immunity may be broader than the protection available even to constitutional court judges.
